digest.component_or_area: completion verifier context assembly and file prefetching
propositions: The completion verifier performs excessive file discovery via repeated read_file and search_files round-trips (84-158 requests per run, 67-82% of distinct reads already named in file_impact), causing 4-6 second latencies that dominate wall-clock time.

Prefetch the verifier's declared file_impact contents plus referencing-commit diffs into the byte-stable leading portion of the fenced context, bounded by 30,000 tokens aggregate and 12,000 chars per file, with skeleton-compression for files over 500 lines to reduce opening discovery overhead.

The close gate (graph=False) must prefetch only the closing ticket's own file_impact (not subtree walk); the deep-review path (graph=True) prefetches subtree-union ranked by cross-descendant frequency; both honor existing graph flag semantics in gate_ops.

Recovery successors receive prefetch via the shared assembled ticket_context (cache-read via byte-stable system_prompt prefix across batched runs), with prefetch bytes included in physical_context_ceiling so oversize prefetch shrinks rather than overflows.

The trusted confirm-against-working-tree rule and skeleton-reread instruction live in completion_verifier.md static prefix before the volatile marker (co-located with prefetch data in both primary and recovery prompts) to prevent re-reading penalty from over-exploration.

Live A/B on real closed tickets (baseline with prefetch disabled vs prefetch enabled) demonstrates at least 20% request reduction with equal verdict class; post-clamp coverage measured per entrypoint (close-path own file_impact 29-33%, graph=True validated against synthetic fixture).
